newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran finds new onshore oil and gas deposits.
newsitem.headline: Iran finds new onshore oil and gas deposits.

text.p: Iran has discovered oilfields containing 3.12 billion barrels of crude in Lorestan province, western Iran, the Kayhan daily newspaper reported on Sunday.
The paper named the fields as Serkan containing 849 million barrels, Malehkooh 941 million barrels, Yazenhar 1.058 billion barrels and Kabood 286 million barrels.
"Serkan and Malehkooh fields have already been exploited, yielding 3,000 barrels daily," Kayhan reported, adding that the crude was being processed at the Kermanshah and Arak refineries.
OPEC-member Iran, the world's third largest oil exporter behind Saudi Arabia and Norway, pumps an average of 3.6 million barrels per day (bpd).
Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh said earlier this year that Iran's proven crude reserves stood at 90 billion barrels, roughly 7.5 percent of global deposits.
Gas fields with exploitable reserves of 53.2 billion cubic meters had also been found in the region, the paper reported.
Iran's gas reserves stand at 21 trillion cubic meters.
